records.tweet_text:
The Rainy Umbrella!

It was a heavy rainy evening in the city. Ada, a 28-year-old teacher, was rushing home after a long day at school. Her feet hurt, her bag felt heavy, and the rain was pouring so hard that her small umbrella could barely keep her dry. 

At the bus stop, she saw a young girl, standing alone under the shelter. The girl had no umbrella and was getting soaked. Her school uniform was wet, and she looked cold and worried.Ada’s heart felt soft. She thought about her own little sister back home and how she would feel if she was out in this rain alone.
Without thinking much, Ada walked over and held her umbrella over the girl too.“Come, stand closer,” Ada said with a kind smile. “We can share.”The little girl looked up with big surprised eyes. “Thank you, Aunty.” They stood together quietly as the rain fell.

 The umbrella was small, so both of them got a little wet on one side, but neither complained. The girl told Ada her name was Nneka and that her mum was late picking her up because of the rain.
When the bus finally came, Ada made sure Nneka got on safely.

 As the girl stepped inside, she turned back and gave Ada a big, bright smile. “You are very kind,” Nneka said. “My mum always says kind people bring their own sunshine on rainy days.” Ada smiled back, even though she was now quite wet. 
She watched the bus drive away, then continued her own journey home.

That night, as Ada dried her hair and drank a warm cup of tea, she felt lighter inside.
Sharing a small umbrella in the rain didn’t cost her much, but it made the heavy day feel softer. 

 Sometimes, the little acts of kindness we give away come back to warm our own hearts the most.

Feel free to share your experience on that act of kindness that lightens your heart?
